messages:
Mira: quick question — for the cost dashboard rollout, are we leaning toward per-invocation amortized credits for prefetch/cache hits, or a sticky 'slab' allocation per route? trying to understand which will map cleanly to token-level unit economics without exploding noise :thinking:
Alex: my vote is amortized per-invocation credits. slab sticky allocations look neat in the UI but make attribution weird when multi-model chains share a cache.
Sahil: +1 to amortized, but we need a defensible math: how do we handle prefix reuse where one request seeds the cache for many later requests?
Carol: we had a quick spike in variance in the simulation last week when we did naive amortization. link to sims: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/UX-cred-sim (internal)
Mira: right — the simulation showed ~30% variance per-tenant when prefetch-heavy routes exist. idea: hybrid approach — emit a per-request "prefetch-credit" (small fixed token credit) and then distribute remaining cache savings across consumers based on last-touch attribution window (e.g., 5m).
Alex: sketch of algo I was thinking of:
```
# on cache fill event
prefetch_credit = min( tokens_saved_estimate * 0.1, MAX_PREFETCH_CREDIT )
record_fill(fill_id, owner_route, timestamp, tokens_saved_estimate - prefetch_credit)
# on cache hit
eligible_fills = find_fills(hit_key, before=hit_ts, within=ATTR_WINDOW)
split = distribute(eligible_fills, by='last_touch_weighted')
charge_each(consumer_route, split_share)
```
Sahil: that looks reasonable. couple questions:
- how do we get `tokens_saved_estimate` cheaply? do we use heuristic (avg token length * default_prefix_len) or real model perf telemetry?
- ATTR_WINDOW default 5m ok? seems small for slow UX routes but large windows hurt causality.

Carol: on the UI side, we should expose both: (1) the prefetch credit line item and (2) the amortized cache savings per route with a confidence band. ops asked for ability to toggle attribution window and see impact in real-time in the console.
Mira: yes — console needs quick toggles. UX mock: "Cache credits: Allocated | Window: 5m | Method: Last-touch (weighted)" with hover explaining formula. Also add a switch to show raw token-level traces for a sample tenant.
billing-bot: automated-sanity-check: comparing month-to-date amortized cache credits vs observed token reductions for a random sample of 1000 sessions: difference = 2.8% (std 0.9%).
Alex: good to see billing-bot sanity. we should run a backfill on last 7 days and produce skew per-tenant. if some tenants have >15% delta, fallback to slab sticky allocation for that tenant (flagged in UI).
Sahil: implementation notes: need a compact fill index keyed by (model_sku, cache_key, fill_ts) and a sliding-window lookup. can reuse existing KV with TTL and incremental aggregates to avoid full scans.
Carol: for rollout, propose opt-in in console: default to amortized for new accounts, and a migration tool that shows tenants how their bill would have changed under each method. must include a CSV export of per-route crediting for finance.
Mira: action items:
- Alex: run 7-day backfill and produce per-tenant delta report (due EOD Tue)
- Sahil: prototype fill-index + attribution lambda, bench at 1k qps (due Fri)
- Carol: add UI mock + toggle + CSV export spec (due Mon)
- I'll draft a short design doc that captures the hybrid algorithm and the fallback rule.
Alex: ack. ping me when the backfill is up, I'll help slice by model_sku and route pattern.
Sahil: noted. starting prototype now, will post perf logs here.
Carol: will attach mocks in the doc, and flag the export endpoints we need from the infra team.
Mira: thanks all — feel free to ping if you want the sim data or the raw traces.
